Cost-DoS attack graph for LLM serving

Attacks, defenses and victims as a directed graph. The middle spine is the request path into an inference engine such as vLLM. Agent clients, training, embodied systems and faintly related work run as parallel lanes that feed into it. Edge thickness counts how many attack papers travel that edge.

Reading the graph

  • Section nodes (rounded boxes) are parts of the system. The thick-bordered ones on the spine are the inference engine path: gateway → admission → scheduler → execution → decode.
  • Lanes are parallel subsystems. Agent clients sit outside the engine and send requests into it. Training changes the weights the engine loads. Embodied systems may call a served model. The related lane holds work that is not compute DoS.
  • Attack papers (dots, colored by family) link to the section where they enter and the sections where they amplify cost. Hollow dots are faintly related work.
  • Defenses (squares) link to the sections they act on. Green border: cheap at high request rates. Amber: moderate. Red: needs an extra LLM call. ✗ marks defenses that were tested and failed.
  • Victims along the bottom show who pays. Turn on "Victim links" or click a victim.

Three questions per attack

  1. Entry: where does attacker-controlled input enter?
  2. Amplifier: where does a small input turn into large cost?
  3. Victim: who pays: the provider, co-located tenants, the bill payer, the end user, or a physical system?

Victim caveat

In direct attacks the attacker sends their own prompt. On a pay-per-token API the attacker pays for it, so the real victims are the provider (on flat-rate, free or self-hosted tiers) and co-located tenants, if the engine's isolation fails. Fill and Squeeze argues continuous batching mostly protects other tenants from long answers, and that their harm comes from KV-cache and scheduler pressure. Injection and agent attacks are different: an innocent party pays.

Nodes marked "read in full" come from papers read in this folder. The rest are classified from arXiv abstracts; verify them before citing. The repo's 110 entries are included; non-LLM domains appear only in the catalog.
